34576-by-violence.title: By Violence
34576-by-violence.creator: John Trevena
34576-by-violence.description: A book by John Trevena. Father Damon stood in a little square room hideously papered. He was small, dark, heavy-featured, peasant-like; and Searell saw at a glance that his successor was as dull in many ways as Oliver Vorse. All that he knew had been forced upon him almost violently; he had not gone forth gathering for himself, he dared not, his mind had been tilled by careful teachers, kept under restraint, all his side-growths pruned away, in order that orthodoxy might develop in one large unlovely head.

arxiv-1901-05340.title: Highlights from the Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) Experiment † \dagger
arxiv-1901-05340.creator: Saranya Samik Ghosh, on behalf of the CMS Collaboration
arxiv-1901-05340.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Saranya Samik Ghosh, on behalf of the CMS Collaboration. The highlights of the recent activities and physics results leading up to the summer of 2018 from the Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) experiment at the CERN Large Hadron Collider (LHC) are presented here.

arxiv-1906-11632.title: A Survey on GANs for Anomaly Detection
arxiv-1906-11632.creator: Federico Di Mattia, Paolo Galeone, Michele De Simoni, Emanuele Ghelfi
arxiv-1906-11632.description: Abstract Anomaly detection is a significant problem faced in several research areas. Detecting and correctly classifying something unseen as anomalous is a challenging problem that has been tackled in many different manners over the years. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and the adversarial training process have been recently employed to face this task yielding remarkable results.

arxiv-2109-15227.title: Yu-Shiba-Rusinov states in a superconductor with topological ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} bands
arxiv-2109-15227.creator: Ching-Kai Chiu, Ziqiang Wang
arxiv-2109-15227.description: Abstract A Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) state is a localized in-gap state induced by a magnetic impurity in a superconductor. Recent experiments used an STM tip to manipulate the exchange coupling between an Fe adatom and the FeTe 0.55 ​ Se 0.45 {\rm FeTe}_{0.55}{\rm Se}_{0.45} superconductor possessing a ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} nontrivial band structure with topological surface states.

arxiv-2111-06714.title: A Review on Communication Protocols for Autonomous Unmanned Aerial Vehicles for Inspection Application
arxiv-2111-06714.creator: Liping Shi, Néstor J. Hernández Marcano, Rune Hylsberg Jacobsen
arxiv-2111-06714.description: Abstract The communication system is a critical part of the system design for the autonomous UAV ( UAV ). It has to address different considerations, including efficiency, reliability and mobility of the UAV. In addition, a multi-UAV system requires a communication system to assist information sharing, task allocation and collaboration in a team of UAVs.

arxiv-2303-09891.title: The role of elastic instability on the self-assembly of particle chains in simple shear flow
arxiv-2303-09891.creator: Matthew G. Smith, Graham M. Gibson, Andreas Link, Anand Raghavan, Andrew Clarke, Thomas Franke, Manlio Tassieri
arxiv-2303-09891.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Matthew G. Smith, Graham M. Gibson, Andreas Link, Anand Raghavan, Andrew Clarke, Thomas Franke, Manlio Tassieri. Flow-Induced Self-Assembly (FISA) is the phenomena of particle chaining in viscoelastic fluids while experiencing shear flow. FISA has a large number of applications across many fields including material science, food processing and biomedical engineering. Nonetheless, this phenomena is currently not fully understood and little has been done in literature so far to investigate the possible effects of the shear-induced elastic instability.

arxiv-2406-08186.title: Hiperwalk: Simulation of Quantum Walks with Heterogeneous High-Performance Computing
arxiv-2406-08186.creator: Paulo Motta, Gustavo A. Bezerra, Anderson F. P. Santos, Renato Portugal
arxiv-2406-08186.description: Abstract The Hiperwalk package is designed to facilitate the simulation of quantum walks using heterogeneous high-performance computing, taking advantage of the parallel processing power of diverse processors such as CPUs, GPUs, and acceleration cards. This package enables the simulation of both the continuous-time and discrete-time quantum walk models, effectively modeling the behavior of quantum systems on large graphs.

arxiv-2502-20141.title: Your contrastive learning problem is secretly a distribution alignment problem
arxiv-2502-20141.creator: Zihao Chen, Chi-Heng Lin, Ran Liu, Jingyun Xiao, Eva L. Dyer *
arxiv-2502-20141.description: Abstract Despite the success of contrastive learning (CL) in vision and language, its theoretical foundations and mechanisms for building representations remain poorly understood. In this work, we build connections between noise contrastive estimation losses widely used in CL and distribution alignment with entropic optimal transport (OT).

arxiv-2504-14881.title: Towards Fuzzing Zero-Knowledge Proof Circuits (Short Paper) Conference: 34th ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis; June 25–28, 2025; Trondheim, Norway 34th ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis (ISSTA Companion ’25), June 25–28, 2025, Tr
arxiv-2504-14881.creator: Stefanos Chaliasos, Imam Al-Fath, Alastair F. Donaldson
arxiv-2504-14881.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Stefanos Chaliasos, Imam Al-Fath, Alastair F. Donaldson. Zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs) have evolved from a theoretical cryptographic concept into a powerful tool for implementing privacy-preserving and verifiable applications without requiring trust assumptions. Despite significant progress in the field, implementing and using ZKPs via ZKP circuits remains challenging, leading to numerous bugs that affect ZKP circuits in practice, and fuzzing remains largely unexplored as a method to detect bugs in ZKP circuits.

arxiv-2506-07458.title: KScope: A Framework for Characterizing the Knowledge Status of Language Models
arxiv-2506-07458.creator: Yuxin Xiao, Shan Chen, Jack Gallifant, Danielle Bitterman, Thomas Hartvigsen, Marzyeh Ghassemi
arxiv-2506-07458.description: Abstract Characterizing a large language model’s (LLM’s) knowledge of a given question is challenging. As a result, prior work has primarily examined LLM behavior under knowledge conflicts, where the model’s internal parametric memory contradicts information in the external context. However, this does not fully reflect how well the model knows the answer to the question.

arxiv-2510-14907.title: Learnable Mixed Nash Equilibria are Collectively Rational
arxiv-2510-14907.creator: Geelon So, Yi-An Ma
arxiv-2510-14907.description: Abstract We extend the study of learning in games to dynamics that exhibit non-asymptotic stability . We do so through the notion of uniform stability , which is concerned with equilibria of individually utility-seeking dynamics. Perhaps surprisingly, it turns out to be closely connected to economic properties of collective rationality.

pmc-12429811.title: General Innovations in Pain Management
pmc-12429811.creator: Alison Deng, Milan Patel, Cole Eigner, Robert Moghim, Alaa Abd-Elsayed, Marco Mercieri
pmc-12429811.description: Chronic pain management is constantly evolving, and our literature review aims to describe the general innovations happening within the field. The need for advancements in chronic pain is a necessity, as debilitating back pain and other forms of chronic pain are significant issues in the United States.

pmc-12466506.title: An Innovative Multi-Omics Approach Reveals the Interactions Between Honeybees and Their Environment
pmc-12466506.creator: Cecilia Rudelli, Elisa Bellei, Giulia Andreani, Gloria Isani, Miroslava Kačániová
pmc-12466506.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummaryIt is becoming increasingly important to evaluate honeybee health in more precise and objective way. This study applied a combined approach of protein and metal analysis to gain a better understanding of how honeybees interact with their environment. The analysis revealed significant variations in the types and quantities of proteins and small molecules present in honeybees from different locations and seasons. Honeybees’ handling of metals such as zinc and copper also varied depending on the location and time of year.

pmc-12476864.title: Selection of suitable wheat genotypes under thermal stress and complex genotype-environment interaction using stability analyses and selection indices
pmc-12476864.creator: Abdelhalim Ghazy, Walid Ben Romdhane, Majed Alotaibi, Abdullah Al-Doss, Omar Dahrog, Nasser Al-Suhaibani, Abdullah Ibrahim, Adel M. Al-Saif, Khalid A. Al-Gaadi, Ahmed M. Zeyada, Khalid F. Almutairi, Ibrahim Al-Ashkar
pmc-12476864.description: Thermal stress is a consequence of climate change that threatens food security, causes plant tissue damage, and harms crop production, particularly during the pollination and fertilization period and in grain-filling stages negatively impacting the number of grains, grain size, and quality.

pmc-13026730.title: Environmental Influences on Food Addiction and Cardiometabolic Profiles in Law Enforcement Officers
pmc-13026730.creator: Yunzhi Qian, Grace E. Russell, Ziyuan Shi, Ya-Ke Wu
pmc-13026730.description: Highlights Public health relevance—How does this work relate to a public health issue? This study addresses how adverse local food environments may exacerbate food addiction and cardiometabolic risk among law enforcement officers, a high-stress occupational group with elevated vulnerability to cardiovascular disease. Public health significance—Why is this work of significance to public health?

pmc-13095259.title: Publication trends of dexmedetomidine and perioperative cognitive dysfunction: A bibliometric analysis from 1995 to 2024
pmc-13095259.creator: Difei Zhou, Lan Yang, Shuai Miao, Xin Zhang
pmc-13095259.description: Introduction:Dexmedetomidine (Dex) has shown potential in mitigating perioperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD). This study aimed to systematically evaluate the research hotspots and development trends in Dex and POCD using bibliometric analysis.Methods:A systematic search was conducted on the Web of Science Core Collection database to identify publications related to Dex and POCD from 1995 to 2024.

pmc-13142762.title: Acute Necrotizing Pancreatitis Due to Hypertriglyceridemia: A Case Report
pmc-13142762.creator: Pranaya Gade, Samantha Walkow, Marina Bastawross, Ayesha Ain, Antonios Tsompanidis
pmc-13142762.description: Necrotizing pancreatitis (NP) is a severe and potentially life-threatening complication of acute pancreatitis (AP). This case report discusses NP in a 39-year-old male patient with severe hypertriglyceridemia (HTG), highlighting management and treatment with supportive measures, intravenous insulin, antibiotic use, and total parenteral nutrition (TPN).

pmc-13372972.title: MOG-Ab-associated optic neuritis with concurrent GFAP-Ab positivity following tislelizumab-based treatment: a case report
pmc-13372972.creator: Yinghui Zhang, Yonghu Liu, Hongxia Xin, Qin Shi, Qiang Liu, Wenna Zhao, Zhuoxiu Qi, Gang Ma, Xiao Yang
pmc-13372972.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo investigate the clinical characteristics and therapeutic management of myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody (MOG-Ab)-related optic neuritis (ON), a rare neurological immune-related adverse event (irAE) associated with the programmed death-1 (PD-1) inhibitor tislelizumab.MethodsWe report a retrospective case of a 48-year-old male patient with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) who developed acute bilateral vision loss after receiving the first dose of tislelizumab combined with chemotherapy.

pmc-13406563.title: Machine Learning for Graduation Prediction in Higher Education: A Systematic Review with a Bio-Inspired Optimization Perspective
pmc-13406563.creator: Andrés Yáñez, Broderick Crawford, Eric Monfroy, Álex Paz, José Barrera-García, Felipe Cisternas-Caneo, Álvaro Peña Fritz, Ricardo Soto
pmc-13406563.description: Timely graduation, time-to-degree, and degree completion are key indicators of student progression and institutional effectiveness in higher education. This study presents a PRISMA-based systematic literature review of machine learning approaches for graduation-related prediction, with attention to predictive targets, pipeline components, scalability, and bio-inspired optimization.
